cands.name: Tasha Boerner
cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the California State Assembly since 2018 and represents the 77th District in coastal northern San Diego County and parts of San Diego. Previously served on the Encinitas City Council. Formerly known as Tasha Boerner Horvath.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Tasha Boerner was born or raised, or when she came to California. Her work history before public office is not documented in the sources we could read. We found no documented actions or stated positions on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration and H-1B, police and public order, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties, or endorsements of her campaign.

qual.background: Member of the California State Assembly since 2018, after serving on the Encinitas City Council. She holds a B.A. in political science from UC Berkeley (1995) and an M.A. in international studies from Claremont Graduate University.

cands.name: Trinity Hannaway
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 77 in 2026. She advanced from the June 2, 2026 nonpartisan primary and faced incumbent Democrat Tasha Boerner Horvath in the general election. The sources I had give no occupation or offices held.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists these endorsements and voter guide recommendations: Reform California, The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn, and several Sway voting groups (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Conservative California, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, Scott's Save Carlsbad Voter Guide).

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Trinity Hannaway was born or raised, when she came to California, or her occupation and work history. She has held no office that we could confirm. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, and we found no campaign website statements, interviews or questionnaires. As a result, we have no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools, policing or donor money. We found no controversies or foreign ties, but the sources were thin, so that is not a finding that none exist.
